newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL END WEEK STEADY AS MAJOR BUYS.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL END WEEK STEADY AS MAJOR BUYS.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges ended the week largely unchanged as a major buyer seeking to cover commitments did a number of deals at the higher end of Thursday's range, traders said.
The major bought up to 5,000 tonnes of refinery product at $95 fob ARA, the same level it purchased at a day earlier and some 50 cents below the highest trade that day.
The major needs material to cover prompt shorts. With product in short supply barge prices have risen close to an unseasonal high of $97.
"If demand continues, we should continue to trade at around $95 but if it wanes we may go down to the $90 level and cargoes will go down in line," a trader with the major said.
Earlier in the day, RMG material was traded a number of times at $94.50 and there was unconfirmed talk of $93.50 done later in the day, traders said.
Traders were mixed about high sulphur cracked fuel cargoes with some saying they were largely steady, talked in the $91/$94 cif region.

However, one trader was reported to be offering a 25,000-tonne loader of utility spec at a high $88 fob, or $3 higher than it paid for it earlier this week, but no buyers were seen at that price level.
For Russian cracked cargoes, traders said that the high end of offers was in the two means plus $2 region, or unchanged. This is $1 lower than their level at the start of the week.
Low sulphur cargo sellers are still sticking to the $96/$97 region, reflecting the level of swaps.
